title: Responder Apprenticeship: Shadowing Curriculum, Handover Checklists, and Customer-Voice Kits
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview:

This document defines a structured Responder Apprenticeship program for new and rotating responders. The apprenticeship combines shadowing, active pairing, formal handover checklists, and a set of reusable customer-voice templates (status page, email, and support chat) tailored for LLM inference incidents (latency, model-quality regressions, KV cache thrash, and capacity blips). The goal is to accelerate operational readiness, reduce noisy escalations, and standardize customer communications while preserving empathetic tone and technical accuracy.

Scope:
- Applicable to all SREs, on-call engineers, platform responders, and solutions engineers participating in on-call rotation.
- Focus areas: detection triage, containment, restoration, post-incident handoff, and customer comms.

Goals and success metrics:
- Time-to-first-meaningful-action (TFMA) for apprentices: target < 10 minutes during supervised shifts (game-day measured).
- Handover completeness rate: > 95% of checklists completed for each incident.
- Customer-template adoption: 100% of external status updates originate from provided kits for incidents with customer impact.

Roles & ownership:
- Program owner: Maya Chen (observability & oncall enablement).
- Lead mentor: Diego Morales (SRE).
- Buddy mentors: platform and runtime engineers assigned 1:1.
- Leadership sponsor: Head of Eng SRE.

Curriculum overview (8-week apprenticeship):
1) Week 0 — Orientation (self-study):
   - Read: incident lifecycle, runbook index, SLOs, and the team Slack triage channel norms.
   - Watch: 2 recorded bridge runs and 1 postmortem walkthrough.
2) Weeks 1–2 — Shadowing (observational):
   - Shadow 4 on-call shifts (night/day mix).
   - Tasks: observe triage, listen on bridge, compile 3 questions per incident.
3) Weeks 3–4 — Paired response (active):
   - Pair with mentor on 6 shifts. Apprentice performs initial triage steps with mentor approval.
   - Mentor checks handover checklist live and completes annotations.
4) Weeks 5–6 — Autonomy with review (semi-independent):
   - Apprentice is primary responder on 4 shifts; mentor acts as observer.
   - After each shift, debrief using the incident evidence template.
5) Weeks 7–8 — Certification & capstone game-day:
   - Participate as primary responder in a scheduled capstone game-day focusing on KV cache/cache-eviction and capacity-throttle scenarios.
   - Pass rubric: TFMA, checklist adherence, communication quality.

Shadowing schedule template (example):
- Day shift: 09:00 - 17:00 PT (2h overlap with mentor; apprentice observes 1 active incident).
- Night shift: 20:00 - 04:00 PT (paired bridge duty; apprentice reduces interruptions).

Handover checklist (must be completed on every responder handoff):
- Incident ID and severity level
- Brief description of symptoms and affected routes/models
- Detection timestamps: first alert, first response, first mitigation
- Actions taken so far (commands, restarts, rollbacks) with runbook links
- Temporary mitigations and known side-effects
- Current hypothesis and next diagnostic steps
- Ownership of long-running tasks and who will follow up (pager + Slack handle)
- Customer-facing status and templates used (link to Customer-Voice Kit)
- Evidence snapshot location (metric dashboards, traces, logs, sample request IDs)
- Suggested postmortem owner and timeline

(Use the following compact table as a quick checkbox for handovers in the bridge):
| Field | Example / Command | Completed? |
| Incident ID | INF-2026-1234 | [ ] |
| Severity | Sev2 - elevated latency | [ ] |
| Affected Model/Route | text-gen:openmodel-6b / embeddings | [ ] |
| Evidence URL | grafana/app?panel=latency | [ ] |
| Temporary Mitigation | scale-up pool, enable prefix-cache | [ ] |

Triage decision ladder (quick reference):
1. Is the issue customer-facing or internal-only? If customer-facing, escalate to on-call lead and prepare a customer template.
2. Can a rollback/model-variant fallback restore acceptable behavior within 10 minutes? If yes, proceed and monitor.
3. If not, apply containment (rate limits, route isolation, revert batching change) and open a mitigation task.

Game-day design (capstone):
- Duration: 3 hours. Scenario mix: KV cache eviction storm, noisy neighbor GPU saturation, model quality regression due to new weights.
- Metrics to monitor: 95th/99th p99 latency, queued requests, GPU util, error-rate per model.
- Evaluation rubric: TFMA, checklist compliance, comms clarity, root-cause reasoning.

Post-incident debrief template (for apprenticeship):
- Summary (one-sentence)
- Timeline (bullet list of key events with timestamps)
- Actions taken and outcome
- What worked / didn’t work (freeform)
- Follow-ups assigned (owner + due date)
- Learning for the apprenticeship curriculum

Customer-Voice Kit (ready-to-use templates)
1) Status page short update (public):
   - Title: Degraded API latency impacting text-generation routes
   - Body: We are investigating elevated latency affecting text-generation endpoints in our hosted region (us-west-2). Some requests may experience delays or timeouts. Our on-call team is actively mitigating the issue; updates will be posted here every 30 minutes.
   - Impact field: Partial outage for text generation; embeddings and non-latency-sensitive routes unaffected.
   - ETA: Initial mitigation expected within 60 minutes.

2) External email template (customers affected by SLA-sensitive incidents):
   - Subject: Incident INF-2026-1234 — Latency impacting inference throughput
   - Body: Hello <CustomerName>,

Our team is investigating an issue impacting inference latency for text-generation routes in us-west-2. We have activated mitigation steps (scaling and prefix-caching) and are monitoring for improvement. We will provide an update within 30 minutes and a post-incident summary once services are stable. If you require assistance or a dedicated bridge, reply to this message and we will escalate.

Regards,
Redwood Inference Ops Team

3) Support chat / CSR quick response (concise):
   - "Thanks for reporting — we're on it. The issue is impacting generation latency; our on-call team is working on containment and we'll update you in ~30m. Can you share any affected request IDs?"

Escalation thresholds (apprentice-specific guidance):
- Immediately page mentor if: TFMA > 20m, severity escalates to Sev1, or rollback risks data loss.
- Notify product/solutions if customer-visible KPI drop > 10% or any enterprise customer reports failures.

Evidence collection checklist (minimal set to attach to postmortem):
- Grafana: latency and request-rate panels (screenshot)
- Traces: 3 representative traces for p99 failures
- Logs: error buckets and a sample of request payloads (sanitized)
- Model artifacts: model version, quantization profile, recent rollout ID

Mentor feedback rubric (pass/fail criteria for certification):
- Technical: correct use of runbooks, evidence collection, and diagnostic commands.
- Operational: follows handover checklist, keeps bridge concise, and documents actions.
- Communication: clear customer updates, correct escalation, and calm bridge facilitation.

Onboarding admin checklist for program owner:
- Assign mentor and buddy within 3 business days of enrolment.
- Schedule game-day in week 8 and reserve a staging cluster for realistic simulation.
- Add apprentice to on-call channel read-only for observational weeks.

References and links:
- Runbook index: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbook-index (internal)
- Postmortem template: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-comm-and-postmortem-framework-2026.json
- Evidence collection standard: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-evidence-chain-and-forensic-runbook-2025.json

Appendix: example diagnostic commands and artifacts to memorize
- Check route health: curl -v https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/health/text-gen
- Snapshot KV cache stats: redis-cli --csv INFO keyspace | grep evicted
- GPU pool utilization: rci gpunode top --pool inference-dedicated
